newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end higher.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked bonds closed higher on Thursday in response to a relatively high December consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.05 pct to 101.39
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 100.86.
Volume was a low 110 million shekels.

"The rise of the Makam and unlinked bonds was very surprising. The Bank of Israel is not expected to lower its base rate following the higher-than-expected December CPI," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.

He said short- and medium-term CPI-linked bonds were the main gainers because of the CPI figure. Released after Wednesday's trading day, the CPI rose 0.8 percent in December, which was at the high end of expectations.

"Yields on unlinked bonds and Makams are too low," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblagon Securities. "Yields on the (one year) Makam fell to 13.8 percent reflecting expectations for a rate cut of one percent, which is simply ridiculous."

Dollar-linked bonds declined as the shekel rose agaisnt the American currency. In the local foreign currency market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2630 shekels against 3.2680 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
